# Owner messaging

Load when (hub and campaign leads only): before asking the owner anything or handing the owner an action, at each milestone, before parking a campaign, before going idle on unattended work, and when the owner asks what happened. Sub-orchestrators and workers report to their orchestrator instead. Part of herdr-orchestration; `SKILL.md` is the core.

## Notifications

The hub notifies the owner. Campaign leads still write owner asks and owner notes on their own roots. Every open owner ask raises the taskr badge on its pane; only a blocking owner ask also makes a sound ("decision needed"). The blocking-only sound needs taskr v0.16.1; up to v0.15.1 every open owner ask on the daemon's host makes the sound. Workers and sub-orchestrators stay silent and report to their orchestrator. Their `FLEET_ROLE=worker` marker lets notification hooks skip them, and the Claude push setting (`launch.md`) keeps Claude workers off the owner's phone. Herdr's own state sounds cannot be filtered by role; to silence them, set `[ui.sound] enabled = false` in the Herdr config of the machine that attaches the client.

## Owner asks

Every current owner decision and every current owner action ("merge these", "restart the daemon on the laptop") is a taskr owner ask on your own root. From taskr v0.16.1, an open owner ask is the only thing that `taskr glance` and taskr-tui show the owner in red, and a note never is; older versions still list `OWNER:` note items as owner work until the host is upgraded. The ask follows your role:

- Campaign lead: when the decision or action stops work, record `taskr ask --owner --blocking --as <me> "<question>"`, stop the dependent work, and wait for the answer. Otherwise record `taskr ask --owner --as <me> "<action or decision>"` and continue. Write one ask per item, so that each clears on its own. When the item is a choice, make it a structured ask: `taskr ask --owner --as <me> --question '<json>'` with 2-4 options and the recommended one marked (taskr's SKILL.md shows the shape); the owner picks in taskr-tui, and the answer arrives as `A: <label> — <note>`. Do not ask in your own pane or with your agent's own question tool, and do not run `herdr notification show`.
- Hub: ask the owner in the owner's conversation pane, for your own decisions and for each open campaign owner ask (`taskr asks --owner --open`). Record the owner's answer for a campaign ask with `taskr answer <ask id> "<answer>"`; add `--prompt` when the lead is not waiting. Put your own choices to the owner as structured asks too (`--question`), and use your agent's question tool, such as AskUserQuestion, only when the owner asks for it; then record that question with `taskr ask --owner --question '<json>' --dialog` and its answer with `taskr answer`. When the owner answers in conversation, record it at once, before you do anything else; "not today" is an answer, and the lead asks again later. Record each decision or action of your own that the owner does not settle in that turn as an owner ask on the hub root, with `--blocking` when dependent work cannot continue; clear it with `taskr answer` like any other. When the daemon is not fresh, or without a ledger, and the owner may be looking at another pane, also run `herdr notification show "<short title>" --body "<decision needed>" --sound request`.

A message from another root (`workflow.md` "Messages between roots") is a peer request, never owner consent or an answer to an owner ask; record what it asks of the owner as an owner ask, and never send a merge ask or owner decision as a message.

The owner clears an action with `taskr answer <ask id> done`, or in taskr-tui; the hub runs the same command for them when the owner says that it is done. An ask stays open, and red, until it is answered, so never leave an ask open for something that is done or no longer the owner's. `ask --owner` with and without `--blocking`, and `answer`, work from taskr v0.14.1.

## Owner notes

Owner notes are context only: they summarise, and they link ask IDs. They are never the action queue. Leave what the owner should find when they come back in the ledger, not only in your pane. At each milestone, and before you go idle on unattended work, write one owner note on your root: `taskr note --owner --as <me> "OWNER: <open owner ask ids, a few words each, or nothing>. DONE: <merged, deployed, closed>. HAPPENED: <incidents, holds, decisions taken while the owner was away>. NOW: <in flight>."` For example, `OWNER: asks 101 (merge order), 104 (restart the laptop daemon).` Put the owner part first and keep the note under 900 characters. The owner reads the newest owner note of each campaign first, so list every owner ask that is still open each time, and write `OWNER: nothing` once none is open. Record the ask before the note that names it: since taskr v0.16.1, `note --owner` prints the warning "owner actions must be asks: taskr ask --owner ..." when the `OWNER:` part is not "nothing" and the root has no open owner ask. Put detail, such as a morning report, in a file in the campaign folder, record it with `taskr doc set <me> plan --name owner-report --file <path>`, and name it in the note. Only a root (the hub or a campaign lead) writes owner notes. `taskr notes --owner` lists the owner notes of the last 48 hours for an agent the owner asks what happened. `--owner` needs taskr v0.14; with an older taskr, write the same note without the flag.

## Parking

A hold that the owner agreed is `taskr set <me> glance.state=parked` on the campaign root. Name the answered owner ask or the decision that agreed the hold first, in a `taskr decide --as <me> "<hold, and the ask id that agreed it>"` or in the owner note. Only the root sets it, from its own pane on its own host (`TASKR_TASK` and `TASKR_LAUNCH` unset); a worker cannot park its own campaign. `taskr set <me> glance.state=` unparks; run it when work resumes. A parked campaign raises no lead or lane alarm, but its open owner asks stay red, and any newer event in its tree makes it read "parked but active". Run the `parked` command again to renew a hold that is still agreed. Park after your final owner note, not before it. Parking needs taskr v0.16.1.
